_dtype_note: bf16 is the v0 reference path and the only one with a pinned correctness tolerance. fp8 and nvfp4 are declared as AXES rather than shipped: the cells exist, their ceilings are computable today, and their reference implementations do not exist yet. Landing one is a cartography contribution and is scored as such -- see docs/CARTOGRAPHY.md. Declaring a cell nobody can run yet is deliberate and is the opposite of overselling: the ceiling table shows the room, and the cell is marked `implemented: false` so nobody mistakes an empty cell for an easy one.
_resolution_note: 512/1024/2048 rather than a denser sweep, because each one has to be CALIBRATED -- a published noise floor per cell costs repeated paired control runs, and a matrix nobody can afford to calibrate is a matrix with guessed floors in it, which is the failure this whole scoring model exists to fix.
_what_this_is: The axes the benchmark declares, and the shape of one receipt. Both are inputs to the screen: the axes decide how much standing unsolved work exists (REGENERATION) and the receipt shape decides what a score costs in GPU time (SCORE_COST). They are configuration rather than constants in the code because a generation that wants a different matrix changes them here and re-runs the screen, and the screen then says whether the new matrix is still affordable.

held_out._rule: Every cell family is scored on its published shape AND on a held-out shape drawn from this list at evaluation time. A candidate whose gain appears on the published shape and vanishes on the held-out one is reported as SHAPE_OVERFIT and credits nothing. The held-out values live here in the open because hiding them would not help -- what makes the guard work is that the evaluator picks which one at run time, from the base commit, after the candidate is frozen.
held_out._what: Shapes that are scored but never published, so a kernel fast only on the benchmarked shape scores nothing.

receipt_shape._cells_note: The three v0 cells at the pinned resolution, both arms, interleaved.
receipt_shape._gate_note: Ten generations for the correctness gate: two determinism replays plus a frozen four-prompt latent comparison, with the first prompt reusing a determinism replay rather than being generated a third time -- same ids, seed, impl, dtype and noise, and proven byte-identical by the replay itself. It runs BEFORE any timing and its cost is part of a receipt whether or not the candidate is fast.
receipt_shape._repeats_note: Three paired interleaved repeats, measured rather than argued down from five. Not two: the paired bootstrap resamples repeat INDICES with replacement, and two indices admit exactly three distinct resamples -- a '99% interval' over them is the larger and the smaller of two numbers wearing a confidence level. Three admit ten, which is coarse and is not meaningless. Three rather than five because resolution is not what this matrix is short of: the base arm's own spread on dit-step measured 0.562% against a published floor of 0.578%, and an effect worth crediting is tens of floors wide. What it IS short of is GPU-hours -- a scoring run costs about half an hour on the pinned part, and a validator pays that per submission. RecurLocal spent nine on its worst cell and the answer was still bimodal, which was a fact about that cell rather than about the repeat count.
